properties.content: Question: what are the symptoms of having worms in humans Answer: Intestinal worms in humans can cause a range of symptoms, from mild to severe, depending on the type of worm and the extent of the infection. Common symptoms include abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea, and vomiting. Other potential symptoms include fatigue, weight loss, loss of appetite, and anal itching, especially with pinworms. In some cases, worms or worm segments can be visible in stool or vomit. Specific Symptoms by Type of Worm:: - Pinworms: Primarily cause anal itching, especially at night, and can lead to insomnia, irritability, and occasional stomach pain. - Tapeworms: May cause nausea, weakness, abdominal pain, and even vitamin deficiencies. Some individuals may pass tapeworm segments in their stool. - Roundworms: Can lead to abdominal pain, fever, and diarrhea. Severe infections can cause more serious complications. - Hookworms: Can cause skin rashes (where they enter the body), abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fatigue. Other Potential Symptoms and Complications:: - Fatigue and Weakness: Worm infections can interfere with nutrient absorption, leading to fatigue and weakness. - Weight Loss: Loss of appetite and nutrient deficiencies can cause unintentional weight loss. - Bloating and Gas: Intestinal parasites can disrupt digestion and cause bloating and gas. - Severe Cases: In rare cases, some worms can cause complications like seizures, vision loss, or even death, particularly in those with weakened immune systems. When to Seek Medical Advice:: It's crucial to consult a doctor if you experience any of the above symptoms, especially if they persist or worsen. A doctor can diagnose the specific type of worm and recommend appropriate treatment.
